findings.title: Team admin/owner check uses AND instead of OR, and denies legitimate admins
findings.body: `isTeamAdmin(...) && isTeamOwner(...)` only passes when the user is both admin and owner. Plain admins are rejected, so the intended permission is wrong. When `teamId` is missing, `?? 0` is passed to the team lookup, which is sloppy. The check should be `isTeamAdmin || isTeamOwner`, and it should be skipped when the event type has no team.

findings.title: Any existing attendee can add guests to a booking
findings.body: `isAttendee` is true for any attendee whose email matches the logged-in user's email, and that alone authorizes adding guests. The UI exposes this action only on the organizer's bookings list, but the tRPC mutation is callable directly. Attendees can then invite arbitrary external emails, which triggers outbound emails and calendar updates sent under the organizer's identity. This is spam and abuse potential. Also, `attendee.email === user.email` is a case-sensitive comparison and ignores secondary or verified emails.

findings.title: Duplicate and blacklist checks are case-sensitive and the input list is not deduplicated
findings.body: The blacklist is lowercased, but `guest` is compared without lowercasing, so `Foo@X.com` bypasses the blacklist. The comparison with existing attendees is also case-sensitive, so the same address in different case is added as a duplicate attendee. Duplicates inside `guests` itself are not removed server-side, because the uniqueness check exists only in the client dialog. Blacklisted or duplicate guests are also silently dropped, and the same raw `guests` list is later passed to the email sender.

findings.title: Emails are sent using the unfiltered `guests` list rather than `uniqueGuests`
findings.body: `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` receives the raw input. A guest that was already an attendee (and was filtered out) or a blacklisted address still counts as a "new guest" in the email logic. Existing attendees therefore get a full "scheduled" email instead of the "guests added" notice. It should be `uniqueGuests`.

findings.title: Calendar update uses the caller's credentials and is unguarded; no guard on booking state
findings.body: `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)` and `new EventManager({...user})` use the logged-in user's credentials. If an attendee or team admin triggers this, the organizer's calendar event is not the one updated. A failure in `updateCalendarAttendees` happens after the DB write and throws after the guests are already persisted, leaving data inconsistent. No check prevents adding guests to cancelled, rejected or past bookings, or to seated events. The `booking.user.credentials` that were loaded are unused. The handler also uses the booking's organizer for the event but the caller's credentials for the calendar.

findings.title: Email failure is swallowed with a bare console.log and no error detail
findings.body: The catch block logs only a constant string and drops the error. The user still sees "Guests added" even if no notifications went out, and debugging is impossible. Use the project logger and include `err`.

findings.title: New guests get the same attendee email, and the logic mis-handles email-disable settings and case
findings.body: `sendAddGuestsEmails` ignores `eventTypeDisableHostEmail` and `eventTypeDisableAttendeeEmail` metadata, so event types that disabled standard emails still send them. `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)` is case-sensitive. The organizer email is sent without any indication of which guests were added. `calEvent.attendees` contains all attendees and the new ones get a scheduled email, so a booking with many attendees triggers a burst of emails.

findings.title: Subject uses attendees[0].name which can be blank
findings.body: The subject uses `this.calEvent.attendees[0].name`. Newly added guests are stored with `name: ""`. The attendee list order is whatever the DB returns, so the subject can render as "Guests Added: X with  at ..." with an empty name. `attendees[0]` could also be undefined in theory.

findings.title: Error toast is malformed and the fallback is unreachable
findings.body: The message is built as `${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}`, which always produces a truthy string such as "BAD_REQUEST: ..." or "undefined: ...". The `|| t("unable_to_add_guests")` fallback therefore never runs, and the raw tRPC code is exposed to users. Also `isInvalidEmail` is never reset on a successful add or when the dialog is closed with the X or Esc.

findings.title: Empty-string emails are not handled before submit
findings.body: The initial state is `[""]`. The `length === 0` check never fires. If the user clicks Add without typing, zod validation fails and the user sees an "unique and valid" message, which is acceptable. But removing every row and clicking Add skips the guard only by accident. The schema is also rebuilt on every render and should live at module scope.

findings.title: Index used as React key and non-localised tooltip text
findings.body: Using `key={index}` for removable inputs causes input state to get mixed up when removing a middle row. The tooltip "Remove email" is hardcoded English instead of using `t()`. The `<label htmlFor="emails">` references no element with that id.

findings.title: Add-guests action shown for all bookings regardless of permission or state
findings.body: The `add_members` action is added to `editBookingActions` unconditionally. It shows for bookings the viewer cannot modify, for past bookings, and for seated events. The label `t("additional_guests")` and id `add_members` are also inconsistent with the feature.
